about: Files 4 and 5 refitted with a separately scaled lower water column (H2O_LOW, the bottom 1 km of the ERA5 profile, below 680 hPa) pinned per file at the median of free fits in the 1.4 and 1.9 um band windows (file 4 -1.5703, file 5 -0.4659), on top of the 2026-10-25 recipe, CO pinned in 4156-4306 as before, 2026-11-09, against the runs it superseded ('canon', now in data/corrected/superseded_pre_lowcol/solar) and photatl's own correction ('authors'). Written by scripts/score_telluric_correction.py --authors photatl --relative-transmission canon=<old run> lowcol=<new run>. The page and pixel sets follow the runs compared, so canon's medians here differ slightly from docs/kitt_peak_clean_1990_score.json's. water_line_cores: residual (observed - model)/continuum at water-only lines (local minima of the published model with 0.15 < T < 0.85, water >= 80% of the optical depth, flat Sun within +-0.1 cm-1), mean within 0.012 cm-1 of the line and rms within 0.06 cm-1, on the same lines in both runs.

ftsspec_901218_4.method: niratl ships the authors' own corrected solar spectrum (Wallace, Hinkle & Livingston 1993). Ours minus theirs mixes both corrections' errors, so instead each is scored on its own, the same way: at pixels where the model transmission is below 0.97 and the solar model is flat (above 0.995 of its continuum), the rms of the corrected spectrum about a running mean of nearby pixels with neither solar nor telluric absorption. A perfect correction leaves noise there. The first and last 50 pixels are not scored: an edge pixel is inside the neighbouring page too (pages overlap by 5 cm-1), and a fit that leaves edges out should not be judged on them. Nor are pixels below a transmission of 0.15, which the corrected products blank: dividing by a saturated core turns a percent of model error into a spike that can outweigh the rest of a window. Two bins: every telluric pixel (T < 0.97) and the deep ones (T < 0.7).
